# Build Keys

## Why a section splits

Paragraph 1. The compiler treats every stage as a pure function of its declared inputs. A build key is the digest of the stage identity, its implementation version, its input digests, the configuration slice it reads, and the schema version it writes. When any of those change the stage runs again; when none of them change the cached artifact is reused verbatim. This is what makes an incremental build honest rather than merely fast. A snapshot records the counts and digests of everything it published, so two builds can be compared without reading their contents.
